PD Ouspensky
In Search of the Miraculous: Fragments of an Unknown Teaching

"when leaving Petersburg at the start of my journey I had said that I was going to "seek the miraculous". The "miraculous" is very difficult to define... I had come to the conclusion that there was no escape from this labyrinth of contradictions in which we live ...beyond the thin film of false reality there existed another reality from which, for some reason, something separated us. The "miraculous" was a penetration into this unknown reality."p.3

"Try to understand what I am saying. Everything is dependant on everything else, everything is connected, nothing is separate. Therefore everything is going in the only way it can go."p.22

"I remember that assertions of this kind made me indignant...people who had passed through any kind of extraordinary experiences and afterwards refused to explain them. They had sought the miraculous...they said"I have found it. But I cannot describe what I have found."p.260-261

"After this G. again passed to the question why we could not tell the story of our lives. And with this the miracle began."p.262

"From there I went into the forest. I walked about there for a long time in the dark., wholly in the power of the most extraordinary thoughts and feelings. Sometimes it seemed to me that I had found something and sometimes that I had lost it again."p.263

"A fairly large company had met together to see him off. He went. But the miraculous was still far from ended. . There were new and very strange phenomena again late in the evening..."p.265

... The first thing I could record was a weakening of that extreme individualism which up to that time had been the fundamental feature in my attitude to life. I began to see people more, to feel my community with them more.... p.266

"It would take a thousand years to study everything."p.15

One was struck by a great inner simplicity and naturalness in him which made one completely forget that he was for us, the representation of the world of the miraculous and the unknown. p.33

he had passed his young years in an atmosphere of fairy tales legends, and traditions. The "miraculous" around him was an actual fact. Predictions of the future which he heard , and which were fulfilled and made him believe in many things.. p.36

The idea of a miracle in the sense of a violation of laws by the will which made them is not only contrary to common sense but to the very idea of will itself. A "miracle" can only be a manifestation of laws which are unknown to men ...A "miracle " is the manifestation in this world of the laws of another world. p.84

The fourth body is composed of material of the starry world, that is of material that does not belong to our solar system, and therefore if it has crystallised within the limits of the solar system, there is nothing within this system that could destroy it. This means that a man possessing the fourth body is immortal within the limits of the solar system.
pages.caption: References: PD Ouspensky

pages.html:
There is a story about an over aged student of a seminary who... does not understand the idea of god"s omnipotence. The examining bishop asks, well give me an example of something the lord cannot do... The students answers "even the lord himself cannot beat the ace of trumps with an ordinary deuce". Nothing could be more clear.... The laws of a game make the essence of the game. A violation of these laws would destroy the entire game. The Absolute can as little interfere in our life and substitute other results of causes created by u or accidentally, as he can beat the ace of trumps with the deuce. p.94-5

The manifestation of the laws of one cosmos in another cosmos constitutes what we call a miracle. There can be no other kind of miracle. A miracle is not the breaking of laws, nor is it a phenomenon outside laws. It is a phenomenon that takes place according to the laws of another cosmos. These laws are incomprehensible to us , and are therefor miraculous." p.207-208

Moreover there is a definite time, a definite term for everything. possibilities for everything exist only for a definite time.
"eternal recurrence" p.251

Every race, every epoch, every nation, every country, every class, every profession has its own definite number of postures and movements. p.351
